extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys and agents, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline, disciplinary authorities, and legal practitioners interested in USPTO reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: An Amended Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing reciprocal discipline on a registered patent attorney, specifying suspension, limited recognition for narrow acts, conditions for reinstatement, and publication/notice obligations. It documents the procedural posture, findings, and regulatory bases for the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Respondent is suspended from practice before the USPTO for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Amended Final Order identifies violation of § 11.804(h) as the immediate regulatory basis for suspension; the record references underlying misconduct found by the Maryland Court as the factual predicate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceeding brought pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 seeking reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a state court (Court of Appeals of Maryland March 16, 2021 order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may impose reciprocal discipline where a state court has disciplined an attorney; the Notice and Order described the request for identical discipline and provided the Respondent the opportunity to oppose under § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within forty (40) days under § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provided Respondent 40 days to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a timely response allows the Office to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and to impose the requested reciprocal discipline (as occurred here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice before the USPTO (scope and commencement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO, with suspension commencing on April 1, 2022.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension covers all practice before the Office (patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters) and specifies an effective start date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigger for meeting 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58(c)-(f)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for Respondent to meet requirements of 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.58(c), (d), (e), and (f) begins to run on the date of the Amended Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 2 sets the procedural starting point for compliance obligations under the cited subsections (which govern trust account and notification requirements, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition for narrow, specified acts (30-day limited recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date the Amended Final Order is signed, expiring thirty (30) days after that date, solely to perform specified acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The limited recognition is narrowly circumscribed to (a) filing a response to the May 17, 2022 Office action in a specified U.S. patent application, (b) responding to the June 17, 2022 Corrected Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due in a specified U.S. patent application, and (c) filing Powers of Attorney executed by the client appointing Respondent for each of the foregoing pending applications. No other practice is authorized under this limited recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable access to USPTO electronic filing system for limited purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Within two days following the date of the Amended Final Order, the USPTO shall grant Respondent reasonable access to the USPTO's electronic filing system used for patent matters for the sole purpose of performing the acts identified in Paragraph 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access is time- and purpose-limited: granted only to enable performance of the specifically authorized filings during the thirty-day limited recognition period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement eligibility and conditions (37 C.F.R. § 11.60 and § 11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent may file a petition for reinstatement as either a patent agent or a patent attorney pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 after one year from April 1, 2022, and upon full compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 and providing proof of completion of a course emphasizing proper maintenance of an attorney trust account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order conditions reinstatement on both the passage of time (one year) and strict compliance with the specific regulatory requirements (§ 11.58). It also allows satisfying the trust-account-course requirement by submitting the proof previously provided to the Maryland authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Amended Notice of Suspension in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish an Amended Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette containing the respondent's name, registration number, the order of suspension, ability to reapply after one year conditioned on compliance with § 11.58, and a narrative summary of the Maryland Court's findings and the misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required notice must summarize the factual and disciplinary basis (including reference to the Maryland order, nature of misconduct, and specific Maryland Rules of Professional Conduct violated), and include availability of disciplinary decisions via the OED FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erratum publishing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish an Erratum in the Official Gazette stating that the prior Notice of Suspension (May 31, 2022 at 1498 OG 558) has been modified and is replaced by the Amended Notice published in this issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Erratum corrects/updates a previously published notice and directs readers to the new Amended Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary authorities and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the states where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures reciprocal and interjurisdictional awareness of the discipline; the Order mandates transmission of the disciplinary information to relevant authorities and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual findings from Maryland Court and Rules violated
rubrics_metrics.description: The Maryland Court found misconduct involving mismanagement/misappropriation-related issues spanning twenty-one personal injury clients; it identified violations of Maryland Attorneys' Rules of Professional Conduct: 1.1, 1.4, 1.15(a), 1.15(b), 1.15(d), 8.4(a), 8.4(c), and 8.4(d). The hearing officer did not make a finding of misappropriation and each client ultimately received owed settlement funds, often belatedly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order incorporates the state-court factual findings and enumerates the specific professional-conduct rules violated as the substantive misconduct supporting reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for action (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the federal statute and regulation authorizing reciprocal discipline and publication/notice obligations; these provisions form the legal basis for the USPTO's actions described in the document.
